question: A 50-year-old man comes to the emergency department for evaluation of right-sided facial weakness that he noticed after waking up. One month ago, he also experienced right-sided neck pain and headache that began after returning from a hunting trip to New Hampshire the week before. He took ibuprofen to relieve symptoms, which subsided a week later. He has a 5-year history of hypertension controlled with drug therapy. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years and he drinks two beers daily. His vital signs are within the normal range. Physical examination shows right-sided drooping of the upper and lower half of the face. The patient has difficulties smiling and he is unable to close his right eye. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

options.opb: Polymerase chain reaction of the facial skin

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Right-sided facial weakness" -> "possible neurological cause" -> "consider stroke or Bell's palsy" -> "recent neck pain and headache" -> "possible infection or inflammatory process" -> "hunting trip in New Hampshire" -> "possible exposure to Lyme disease" -> "Cerebrospinal fluid analysis to check for Lyme disease" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Right-sided facial drooping" -> "indicates lower motor neuron lesion" -> "could be due to Bell's palsy or stroke" -> "recent symptoms of neck pain and headache" -> "suggests possible infectious or inflammatory etiology" -> "hunting trip raises suspicion for Lyme disease" -> "Cerebrospinal fluid analysis to confirm Lyme disease" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Facial weakness and drooping" -> "suggests cranial nerve involvement" -> "recent history of neck pain and headache" -> "could indicate viral or bacterial infection" -> "hunting trip suggests possible tick exposure" -> "Cerebrospinal fluid analysis to rule out Lyme disease" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with right-sided facial weakness" -> "indicates potential neurological issue" -> "recent neck pain and headache" -> "could suggest an infectious process" -> "hunting trip in New Hampshire" -> "increased risk for Lyme disease" -> "Cerebrospinal fluid analysis is appropriate for diagnosis" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation of right-sided facial weakness, along with a history of neck pain and headache after a hunting trip, raises suspicion for a possible cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or other neurological condition. Given the acute onset of facial weakness and the risk factors present (hypertension, smoking), a noncontrast CT scan is the most appropriate next step to rule out any acute intracranial pathology such as a stroke. Other options like CSF analysis or serological tests are not immediately indicated in this acute setting. Therefore, a noncontrast CT is the best choice for initial evaluation.
normal_results: Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay DIAGNOSES Cerebrovascular accident
